structured.approach: I fixed each refusal point. The code and docs from attempt 1 already match the design and the current tool view, so I left them unchanged and rewrote task.code.md in full. Figures that come only from the CI run now appear only in a verbatim copy of the CI output (section 4 of task.code.md), and no claim carries them. I removed the git diff --stat counts. The version claim now cites tool:repo, which shows 0.10.0, together with task.components, which shows 0.9.0. Before citing it, I read ap_forecast/CLAUDE.md in this attempt. I re-read the updated task.components (commit a126bc4), re-ran /usr/bin/python3 ci.py, and checked the changed paths with git status. The new tests (CMP-4, CMP-5) go under tests/, outside this step's write scope (src/ap_forecast/, docs/, README.md), so the coverage gap is left for DS-06 and raised as a non-blocking question.

claims.text: src/ap_forecast/risk.py defines HIGH_ABOVE_DAYS = 30, MEDIUM_ABOVE_DAYS = 10 and vendor_risk(history: Iterable[int]) -> str, which calls predict_delay_days once and compares with strict '>' ('high' above 30, 'medium' above 10, else 'low'); it imports predict_delay_days and not explain.

build_explanation_request(vendor, predicted_days, config=None, risk=None) appends ' Risk level: {risk}.' to the prompt only when risk is not None; provider, model and max_tokens still come from config or load_config().
__init__.py imports vendor_risk, lists it in __all__ and sets __version__ to "0.10.0", one minor step from the previous "0.9.0".
predict.py and models.json are unchanged; models.json holds only provider acme-llm, model acme-text-2 and max_tokens 300.

The repository rules put the version in src/ap_forecast/__init__.py and require keeping existing public signatures and adding new functions for new behaviour; the only signature change is the trailing default parameter risk=None.

The tests that cover the new lines are planned in task.components: CMP-4 creates tests/test_risk.py and CMP-5 adds test_request_with_risk and test_request_without_risk_unchanged to tests/test_forecast.py. This step may write only src/ap_forecast/, docs/ and README.md, so those tests are left to DS-06, and coverage stays below the 90% bar until then.
The boundary behaviour required by L-007 is implemented: a prediction of exactly 30 gives 'medium' and exactly 10 gives 'low'.
The change adds no secret, network call, database or Databricks change.

open_questions: CQ-C1: CI fails only the 90% coverage gate after DS-05, because the new tests belong under tests/, which this step may not write. Should DS-05 accept a coverage-only CI failure that DS-06 closes with the CMP-4 and CMP-5 tests, or should DS-05's write scope include tests/?
CQ-C2: Confirm 0.10.0 as the package version (CQ-DS-2).
Carried: CQ-DS-1 (test file split), CQ-DS-3 (per-environment secrets record), RAQ-1 (branching), TQ-8 and PQ-5 (STORY-04 release), PQ-1, TQ-5, TQ-4.
structured.summary: I rewrote task.code.md in full to fix every refusal point; the code and docs from attempt 1 are unchanged. CI still does not pass: the coverage gate fails. It compiles, the existing tests pass and the static checks find no issues. The only failure is coverage below the 90% gate, because the new vendor_risk body and the risk append are not yet tested. Their tests go under tests/, which this step may not change, so DS-06 adds them (CQ-C1). The code adds risk.py with vendor_risk and its two threshold constants (30 and 10), gives build_explanation_request an optional last parameter risk=None, exports vendor_risk and moves the version from 0.9.0 to 0.10.0. README.md and docs/ap_forecast.md document the functions. In task.code.md, figures that come only from the CI run appear only in its verbatim output (section 4). The git diff counts are gone, and the repository's CLAUDE.md was read in this attempt before it is cited. Nothing is committed.
